I have $642 and four unmortgaged properties. p1 is the main threat with a massive empire and GOOJF card. I am essentially playing a one-on-one game against p1.

p1 has four houses on every major color group. The bank is empty of houses but holds twelve hotels. I have a dark blue monopoly, yet Park Place is mortgaged and the bank cannot build. I am deciding between ending the turn, proposing a trade, or adjusting mortgages.

I am weighing whether to unmortgage Park Place. The cost is roughly $212. I need cash for orange hits. I will keep Kentucky Avenue to block reds.

Unmortgaging Park Place would cost about $193 and leave me with roughly $449. The combined rent from both dark blues is only about $170, which is not enough to threaten p1's $388. I am now checking the board positions to see how close p1 is to Park Place.

p1 at Connecticut Avenue must travel almost the entire board to reach Park Place. I am now calculating the possible rolls from Oriental Avenue.

Rolling from Oriental Avenue lands on Vermont, Connecticut, Jail, St Charles, and Electric Company. Vermont is an unmortgaged light blue owned by p1, so rent is $6 rather than doubled. Connecticut and St Charles are mortgaged and pay no rent. I own Electric Company.

Rolling 6 from Oriental lands on States (mortgaged) and 7 on Virginia (unowned). Penn RR is owned by p1, but Short Line is mortgaged. I am checking whether mortgaged railroads still count toward the rent multiplier.

Mortgaged railroads do not count toward the rent multiplier. The next rolls from Oriental Avenue include St James, Tennessee, and New York, each with four houses and rent of $750, $750, and $800. The probability of hitting an orange property is roughly 19%.

I can survive an orange hit by mortgaging my properties. Unmortgaging Park Place now would shrink that cushion and freeze the dark blue set if I later need to mortgage Boardwalk. I am also considering trading with p1 for houses, since I cannot build without them.

Trading with p1 is too risky. They hold three monopolies at four houses and would not give up their assets easily.

I must keep Kentucky Avenue. It blocks p1 from completing the red group if they buy Indiana, Illinois, and Virginia.

Boardwalk and Park Place are my only winning combination. I should not offer either to p1.

p1 owns all 32 houses on their properties. I need those houses returned to the bank before I can build on my dark blues.

p1 might replace four houses with a hotel to return them to the bank. That would let me build on my dark blues. But hotels would also raise orange and green rent to $950–$2000. I need to hit p1 before bankruptcy while I still have enough cash.

I am now in a grim position. p1 has the board locked and I am about to walk into their orange gauntlet. Unmortgaging Park Place would cost cash I need for survival. Mortgaging now would reduce my income without immediate benefit. I am now looking for a trade that could create a win.

I cannot trade houses directly. p1's GOOJF card is not worth enough to offer in exchange. I have no partial monopolies to complete, and my dark blue set is already fully owned.

I will end the turn and stay liquid. I am not trading with p1 because they would only accept deals that benefit them. I am also checking whether this is my post-roll position after a roll from Oriental Avenue.
